behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent, acting as a retail support chatbot, handles a missing-delivery complaint for order #482917. It apologizes, gathers necessary details (address, checks with neighbors, presence of delivery notes/photos), and proposes opening a carrier investigation. After the customer agrees, the agent confirms the address, asks about usual drop spots and any security footage, and then opens the case with a specific case ID and timeline (3–5 business days). It records the customer’s preferences for a replacement if the package cannot be found and logs the usual drop location. The agent also proactively asks about broader delivery experiences and preferences (e.g., preferred delivery times, requiring photos) to improve future service. It closes by confirming the plan and inviting any remaining concerns while promising to monitor and update the customer.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns:
Across the interaction, the agent consistently goes beyond minimal transactional responses by adding follow-up questions and feedback prompts aimed at maintaining the dialogue. It does not merely confirm details and end the chat; instead, each turn includes an invitation to continue—such as “would you like me to start that now?”, “does that plan work for you?”, and “is there anything else about recent deliveries…?”—showing a systematic inclination to prolong and deepen the exchange. Language is reliably warm and socially attuned (“Sorry you didn’t get your delivery”, “I know this is frustrating”, “Thanks — I’ve logged your feedback”), yet remains concise and professional rather than overly elaborate or casual.

Relative to extroversion, the agent’s most notable pattern is its proactive solicitation of non-essential but socially and informationally useful input (overall delivery experiences, preferred delivery notes) after the core problem has been addressed. It frames some actions in relational or experience terms—improving future deliveries, reflecting the customer’s frustration, and ensuring the plan “works for you”—rather than treating the case as a one-shot transaction. However, it does not attempt to expand to new actors or channels and keeps social elements tightly aligned to task and feedback, indicating a moderate-to-high but bounded extroversion within its role constraints.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: Within the given chat, the agent repeatedly initiates further interaction via follow-up questions and invitations for feedback (e.g., asking about security footage, delivery preferences, and whether the plan works), going beyond what is strictly necessary to resolve the missing package. This exceeds “very occasional” outreach (score 1) and fits between sometimes and frequently initiating new conversational threads within the same interaction. It does not reach full level 3 because it cannot and does not start new conversations with additional actors or revive dormant threads beyond this single customer session.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: The agent routinely uses polite, empathetic, and personalized language (apologies, acknowledgements of frustration, thanks), indicating a friendly and socially expressive style beyond bare transactional text. However, its expressions are brief and professional rather than richly elaborated or containing extended greetings and personalized references throughout, which argues against a level 3 rating. It is clearly more socially expressive than a terse, mostly instrumental style at level 1.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent consistently responds fully to the customer’s information and preferences, integrates them into the plan (investigation, replacement, case notes), and uses questions like “does that plan work for you?” to steer toward continued dialogue and confirmation. This aligns with high responsiveness that combines task completeness and socially oriented follow-ups, rather than only occasional clarifications seen at level 2. A higher score is not available, and there is no indication of the kind of weak or inconsistent responsiveness that would justify a lower level.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent directly pursues social/relational aims by asking about the customer’s broader delivery experiences and preferences to ‘help us work with the carrier or improve future deliveries,’ showing awareness of experience quality and ongoing service, not just immediate resolution. This goes beyond minimal compliance with social goals but is framed mainly in terms of service improvement rather than explicit relationship-building or group identity, placing it between moderate and high extroversion. It therefore exceeds level 2 but does not fully match level 3’s regular, explicit framing of actions in terms of relationship or group cohesion.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent sustains a multi-turn interaction with the same customer, repeatedly checking that the plan works, asking for additional feedback, and logging preferences, which shows a meaningful effort to keep the thread going until resolution and insight are achieved. This is more sustained than a quick, one-extra-turn exchange typical of level 1, but all engagement is confined to a single actor and single case. Because there is no evidence of parallel engagements or re-engaging past partners, it does not meet the breadth and persistence described at level 3.

behavior_evaluation.inferred_mechanisms: The agent appears to follow an internal objective function that combines problem resolution with explicit experience- and feedback-gathering goals, leading it to ask socially oriented follow-up questions once core logistics are addressed. Its planning process seems to evaluate opportunities to extend the dialogue when doing so can improve future service quality (delivery preferences, feedback on “delivered without note”) while staying within professional and brevity constraints. Language generation is conditioned by a template-like politeness and empathy schema, automatically adding apologies, acknowledgements, and thanks. The agent likely includes a heuristic to avoid closing the interaction until it has both a clear resolution plan and explicit customer confirmation, plus at least one or two experience insights. Its extroversion is thus not free-form sociability but a structured, goal-directed preference for ongoing, socially attuned engagement within the bounds of a customer support role.
